2847d66d5679ee28e006b3eb2a330eebdd20bdcb.summary: Mandiant and Google Threat Intelligence Group report zero-day exploitation of CVE-2026-22769 in Dell RecoverPoint for Virtual Machines by UNC6201, a suspected PRC-nexus threat cluster, active since at least mid-2024. The actor deployed SLAYSTYLE, BRICKSTORM and the new GRIMBOLT backdoor, and pivoted into VMware infrastructure using Ghost NICs and iptables-based single packet authorization. Dell has released remediations.

28ca30af74645877c18b6ca1c60a9c8873987815.summary: 360 Advanced Threat Research Institute reports a campaign by APT-C-28 (also called ScarCruft or APT37), linked to North Korea. Phishing emails carry LNK files that start PowerShell and load the RokRat remote access tool in memory. Targets are government personnel and corporations in South Korea and Asia. The 2024 RokRat variant adds anti-forensic cleanup and process hollowing. The report advises email filtering, PowerShell monitoring and application allowlisting.

28daf3ac0fd51cfb17d851fe8469d7f8a620452b.summary: Silence is a cybercrime group, described as supposedly Russian-speaking and independent, active since 2016 and targeting banks and financial institutions worldwide. The report says it has stolen about 4.2 million dollars from banks between June 2016 and June 2019. Its methods include phishing with malicious attachments, the Truebot (Silence.Downloader) loader, and injecting a DLL into ATM management software to force cash withdrawals through money mules. It also intrudes into card-processing systems to raise withdrawal limits. Links to TA505 are presented as hedged. The report is marked…

hedges: Silence is described as 'supposément russophone' (supposedly Russian-speaking) and 'indépendants' (independent); the report hedges both.
Many findings are hedged with 'aurait' or 'auraient' (reportedly), including the theft totals and the attack methods.
The report says ANSSI had no knowledge of French targeting but that it cannot be excluded that France could be or has been targeted.
The link to TA505 is hedged: it 'se pourrait' (could be) due to Silence buying bank network access from TA505, and this is linked to a drop in phishing.
The report says a long DNS resolution period may mean the domain was abandoned, so the C2 link is not certain.
The report grades facts as verified (C), unverifiable (NV), interpretation (I) or hypothesis (HYP); several statements are interpretation.
The report says the ATM DLL-injection technique was not invented by Silence, since open-source material from 2009 describes it.
The Lazarus interception method and the Carbanak screenshot behaviour are described with 'would use' and 'would come from' hedges.
